findings.bug: Diff swapped the guarded `update(Batch).where(Batch.status == BatchStatus.OPEN)` + `rowcount == 1` check for a plain ORM write (`batch.status = final; if batch.callback_url: _queue_callback(...)`). The open check is now a Python read at line 44, with no compare-and-swap.
findings.repro: 1) POST /batches, 2 jobs, callback_url set. 2) Workers W1 and W2 each claim one job. 3) Both call /worker/jobs/{id}/complete at about the same time, and each commits its job before its on_job_finished runs. 4) Both db.get(Batch) see OPEN and both count succeeded=2. 5) Both flush UPDATE batches with no status filter and both _queue_callback, so 2 batch.callback jobs land on queue 'callbacks'. Variant: a finisher whose counts are stale (a manual retry happens in between) writes COMPLETED over COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS, and the two callbacks report different statuses.

findings.bug: run_after accepts a timezone-aware datetime and build_job stores it as is. The SQLite DateTime type (and Postgres timestamp without time zone) drops the offset without converting, but the claim filter compares against naive UTC from utcnow().
findings.repro: 1) POST /jobs with {"queue":"q","kind":"k","run_after":"2026-11-17T10:00:00+05:30"} (04:30 UTC). 2) It is stored as 10:00 and read as UTC. 3) /worker/claim at 05:00 UTC returns 204, and the job stays delayed 5.5h past the requested time. A negative offset makes it run early.

findings.bug: `if key:` treats "" as no key and skips the pre-select, but build_job still stores idempotency_key="". The unique constraint then makes "" act as a real key through the IntegrityError path.
findings.repro: 1) A client sends POST /jobs {"queue":"q","kind":"a","idempotency_key":""}, which returns 201 job 1. 2) Later it sends POST /jobs {"queue":"q","kind":"b","payload":{...},"idempotency_key":""}. 3) The flush raises IntegrityError, the code rolls back and refetches, and the call returns 200 with job 1 (kind a). Job b is never created.

findings.bug: The manual retry resets status, attempts, run_after, finished_at and last_error. It keeps lease_owner (complete_job never clears it), started_at and the previous run's JobOutput rows.
findings.repro: 1) W1 claims and completes job 7 with output {rows:10}, and lease_owner stays 'W1'. 2) The tenant calls POST /jobs/7/retry. 3) GET /jobs/7 shows status=queued, lease_owner='W1', started_at from the old run. 4) GET /jobs/7/outputs returns [{rows:10}] for the queued job. After the re-run it returns 2 outputs with no attempt marker, so the client cannot tell which one is current.

findings.bug: Diff dropped `this.generation++` from stop(). Now stop() does not cancel a getJob already in flight. The generation guards at lines 69/78 still pass, so after stop that call writes job/error, re-arms the timer at line 83 and can call onFinished.
findings.repro: 1) watch('j1'), with before-hook holding getJob. 2) User stops (or the timer callback has already fired and check is awaiting). 3) stop() sets polling=false and clears timer=null. 4) getJob resolves with status running: generation still matches, job is written, new timer scheduled, and polling carries on with polling=false. 5) Backend sets succeeded: onFinished(job) fires on a poller the user stopped. If getJob throws instead, error is written to the stopped chip.
